subject.title: fix(transcripts): imported text can inject terminal escapes through transcripts show

question: Should OpenClaw approve the security boundary where untrusted session IDs remain raw in stored metadata but terminal-facing list selectors use the store’s safe directory segment?
rationale: This fixes terminal injection while intentionally changing the observable selector for unusual external IDs; the code and proof support the approach, but the permanent CLI compatibility contract needs the assigned reviewer’s judgment.

options.title: Approve the presentation boundary
options.body: Accept raw IDs as storage identity and safe directory-backed selectors as the terminal and copy/paste contract for externally supplied control-bearing IDs.

options.title: Preserve raw list identifiers
options.body: Keep the old first-column contract and add a separately named safe selector field or mode, accepting the additional interface and maintenance surface.

recommendation.title: Approve the presentation boundary
recommendation.body: Accept raw IDs as storage identity and safe directory-backed selectors as the terminal and copy/paste contract for externally supplied control-bearing IDs.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned and raised the precise JSON terminal-control boundary issue on this PR.
